about.label: About
about.headline: One app. One clear path. One step at a time.
about.paragraph: Amigro is a mobile app for people who have just arrived in Germany. German bureaucracy is complex and mostly in German, which leaves many newcomers anxious, unsure where to start and at risk of mistakes with real consequences. Amigro brings all the first steps together in one checklist, in the order they need to happen, so users always know what comes next. For every appointment, a packing list shows exactly which documents to bring, so nobody is sent away and has to start again.
about.reviewNote: TO VERIFY: The checklist is a guide, not a fixed order. Check health insurance and residence requirements right away. Document lists are starting lists, not complete requirements for every situation. The tax ID step has no documents to bring for automatic allocation.

faq.question: Who is it for?
faq.answer: Migrants and newcomers in their first weeks in Germany.

faq.question: Where?
faq.answer: Starting with Berlin, with more cities to follow.

faq.question: Do I need every step?
faq.answer: Not always. The residence permit, for example, depends on your nationality.

faq.question: Which documents do I need?
faq.answer: Every step lists the documents to bring with you.

faq.question: I arrived a few months ago. Is it still useful?
faq.answer: Yes, tick off the steps you already did and see what is still missing.

faq.question: What about deadlines?
faq.answer: Amigro tells you which steps have a deadline and why it matters.

faq.question: Legal advice?
faq.answer: No, every step links to the official source.

steps.title: Register your address (Anmeldung)
steps.whyItMatters: Registering your Berlin address gives you an official registration confirmation for later administrative steps.
steps.timing: Register within 14 days of moving into your main or only home in Berlin. TO VERIFY: Whether a short-stay exception or legal deadline adjustment applies to you.
steps.packingListNote: For an in-person appointment, bring originals of the required identity documents, the signed housing provider confirmation and the completed registration form. A rental contract does not replace the housing provider confirmation. TO VERIFY: Extra documents for your household.
steps.timingShort: Usually within 14 days of moving in
instructions: Check the official checklist for your household.
Book a Bürgeramt appointment for an in-person registration. TO VERIFY: Check whether you qualify for online registration.
Have the listed documents ready, then keep your registration confirmation.

steps.title: Receive your tax ID (Steueridentifikationsnummer)
steps.whyItMatters: Your tax ID identifies you for tax matters and stays with you for life.
steps.timing: After your first address registration in Germany, your tax ID is assigned automatically and sent by post. TO VERIFY: Delivery time and when to request a missing letter.
steps.packingListNote: Nothing to bring for automatic allocation after registration. If you already have a German tax ID, keep that number. TO VERIFY: The information needed if you request a missing letter.
instructions: Make sure your address registration is complete.
Look out for the tax ID letter by post. Keep an existing German tax ID if you already have one.
TO VERIFY: If the letter is missing, check the current BZSt process before requesting it again.

steps.title: Arrange health insurance (Krankenversicherung)
steps.whyItMatters: Health insurance is compulsory in Germany and helps cover the cost of medical care.
steps.timing: Arrange continuous cover from your first day in Germany, including any gap before employment or regular insurance starts; do not wait for Anmeldung. TO VERIFY: Which cover is accepted for your status.
steps.packingListNote: TO VERIFY: Ask your insurer which identity, employment or study documents and previous-insurance details it needs; family cover may require extra evidence. Requirements depend on your circumstances.
instructions: Check that you have continuous cover from your first day in Germany.
TO VERIFY: Ask the insurer which type of cover fits your status and when it starts.
TO VERIFY: Request your personal checklist and confirmation of cover.

steps.title: Arrange a bank account (Girokonto)
steps.whyItMatters: A suitable bank account helps you receive income and pay rent and everyday bills.
steps.timing: Arrange an account when you need it for income, rent or bills. TO VERIFY: Whether your existing account is sufficient, and whether your chosen bank requires Anmeldung before opening an account.
steps.packingListNote: Have your valid passport or another identity document accepted by the bank ready. TO VERIFY: The bank may also request proof of address, a visa or residence document, tax ID or proof of income; get its current checklist.
steps.timingShort: When you need it for payments
instructions: TO VERIFY: Check whether your existing account meets your needs and ask your chosen bank for its document checklist.
Follow the bank’s application and identity check process.

steps.title: Check the broadcasting contribution (Rundfunkbeitrag)
steps.whyItMatters: One broadcasting contribution normally covers one dwelling, so checking who pays helps you avoid duplicate payments.
steps.timing: After moving in, check whether someone already pays for your dwelling before registering or responding to a contribution-service letter. TO VERIFY: Your registration deadline, payment start date and any exemption or reduction.
steps.packingListNote: Have your address and move-in date, any contribution-service letter and the existing household contribution number, if someone already pays, ready for the online forms. TO VERIFY: Special accommodation rules and evidence for an exemption or reduction.
instructions: Check whether someone already pays for your dwelling.
Use the official contribution service to register or respond to a letter.
TO VERIFY: Check whether an exemption, reduction or special accommodation rule applies.

steps.title: Check your residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis)
steps.whyItMatters: The appropriate residence permission allows you to stay in Germany for the purpose and period it covers.
steps.timing: Check immediately, even though this step is listed last. TO VERIFY: Whether you need to apply, your application window and the deadline before your current permission to stay expires.
steps.packingListNote: TO VERIFY: Prepare the documents on the official checklist for your exact residence route; the items here are a starting list, not a complete or universal requirement.
steps.applicabilityNote: For non-EU newcomers only. TO VERIFY: Non-EU nationality does not automatically mean this permit is required; EEA citizens, Swiss citizens, family members and people whose visa covers their entire stay may follow different rules.
instructions: TO VERIFY: Find the residence route for your nationality and purpose of stay.
Open Berlin’s official service list. Use the online application for your route if available; otherwise follow the contact instructions.
TO VERIFY: Confirm your exact application deadline and document checklist.
